best_for: Windows users whose drive is suddenly full and who want to see at a glance which folders and files are taking the space.
description:
SpaceSniffer is a disk space viewer written by Umberto Uderzo, who says he made it because he wanted a tool he would not have to learn again each time he opened it. Its block layout is a treemap, an idea from Professor Ben Shneiderman, who gave permission to use it.

You do not have to wait for a scan to finish: you can move around while it runs, and open several views of the same disk with different filters from a single scan. When files change, the view updates and the changed blocks blink. Right-click a block to get the normal Windows file menu, rescan a zoomed area on its own, or look into NTFS alternate data streams. Colors, layout and behavior can be adjusted.

points.title: Space as a map
points.text: It draws your drive as blocks sized by how much they use, so the biggest folders stand out at once. Click a block for details or double-click to zoom into it.

points.title: Filters that answer real questions
points.text: Type `*.jpg` to show only photos, put `|` in front to hide a type, or filter by size or age such as `>2years`. Combine several with semicolons to find old, large files fast.

points.title: Tag and report
points.text: Mark files red, yellow, green or blue with keyboard shortcuts, then filter by tag. An export module writes a text report with a layout you can adjust.

points.title: No installer at all
points.text: SpaceSniffer is portable: it comes as an x64 zip you unpack and run. Nothing is added to Windows, which suits a USB stick or a locked-down PC.

points.title: Freeware, Windows only
points.text: It is free with donations welcome, but it is closed source and there is no Mac or Linux version. The publisher's page does not list supported Windows versions.

points.title: Four versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 4 versions, so you can go back if a new build misbehaves.
